notes: Inbound SMB lead. Product: event-driven customer notifications (transactional + campaign blasts). Typical traffic pattern: steady low-rate churn for transactional messages, periodic large spikes when marketing campaigns and nightly digest jobs run (approx 10k events over 10-15 minutes in test environment). Customer reports seeing intermittent 429s on other APIs and wants deterministic behavior. Key asks: clear per-minute and concurrency quotas, documented retry/backoff pattern, and simple self-serve way to lift burst capacity during campaign windows. Cost sensitivity: low-to-mid; wants to understand unit economics of burst versus reserved capacity. Quote from CTO: "We need predictable tails during campaigns — missing notifications is visible to customers. If we can’t handle short spikes we’ll need to build queuing infra which defeats the point of using a hosted API." Wants examples of safe retry jitter and a sample rate-limiter implementation. Open to simple caching/prefix reuse for repeated templates. Technical constraints: NodeJS backend on AWS, currently no SSO. Interested in hosted API as first step; may evaluate Dedicated later if costs for repeated spikes are high. Action items: provide sample script, recommended concurrency-per-key defaults, and show how quota increases are handled via console or support ticket. POC should simulate 3x, 5x, and 10x normal peak to validate 429 behavior and latency under load.
use_case_summary: Use hosted API to generate templated notification content for emails, in-app messages, and support responses. Primary concern is graceful handling of traffic spikes without losing messages or incurring runaway costs.
integration_notes: Backend: NodeJS using async batch workers. Proposed approach: client-side rate limiter, exponential backoff + jitter, server-side batching where applicable, and temporary quota bump for campaign windows. They want a one-file example they can drop into their worker process.
sales_notes: SMB inbound, strong product-market fit for quick win. Self-serve funnel is working; next milestone is POC. Upside: convert to monthly committed spend if POC proves stable. Risk: cost sensitivity may push them to open-source runtime if hosted burst pricing looks unfavorable.
